pr.title: Name an older daemon from `trip screen`, and say how to switch back after a mismatched upgrade
pr.head: d4b11af19c0c15bf14459d5e2ada3cbd162c4b4f

summary: trip runs a long-lived daemon that holds every terminal session, and the trip command is a client that sends it one request per invocation. Because trip upgrade never restarts the daemon, a newer client often talks to an older daemon. When that daemon cannot decode a request, it closes the connection without replying. The previous pull request, #31, taught the client to turn that close into one line naming the older daemon and saying when it moves to the new version.
This pull request follows up two suggestions from that review:

1. trip screen and trip log now name an older daemon. trip screen used to treat a close before any reply as success, so against an older daemon it printed nothing and exited 0. A current daemon always replies to a screen request before it closes, so that close is now an error, and the older-daemon line explains it. trip log still exits 0, because a current daemon also closes without replying when a log has no events. But it now prints the older-daemon line to stderr when the daemon is older.
  2. A mismatched upgrade says how to switch back. When trip upgrade installs a build that reports a version other than the release tag's, the installer has already made that build current. The error now says so and gives the ln -sfn command back to the version the upgrade replaced. When the build reports the version already running, the installer reinstalled it over itself, and the error says it is still current, with no command.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Older daemon: a running daemon whose version, recorded in ~/.trip/daemon.json, is lower than the client's.
  • current and previous: symlinks in ~/.local/share/trip. current names the installed version, and ~/.local/bin/trip runs through it. previous names the version current named before the installer last switched it to a different version.
  • Mismatch: the release tag says one version and the build it installs reports another.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at 2d2bbd3, found one P2: when the mismatched build reported the running version, the switch-back command named an older version and would have downgraded. This head fixes it by reading current before the installer runs, and the author resolved the thread.
  • This head also takes both suggestions: an older-daemon line for an empty trip log, and an e2e case for trip screen --watch of a session that ends.
  • The review of d4b11af is clean.

groups.title: trip screen and an older daemon
groups.kicker: A close before the first reply is now an error for trip screen, and a warning for trip log.
intro: get_screen reads replies from the daemon until the connection closes. In watch mode it prints each new screen, so a close after a reply means the session ended and is a normal exit. A close before any reply only happens when the daemon refused the request, so that case now fails with unexpected frame. main.rs already passes every request's error through explain_daemon_failure, which turns unexpected frame into the older-daemon line when the daemon is older.

get_log cannot fail the same way. The daemon's GetLog handler writes nothing when there are no events to show and then closes, so an empty log and a refusal look identical to the client. Instead, on a close before any LogData, it calls warn_if_daemon_older, which prints the older-daemon line to stderr only when the daemon's record names an older version, and then exits 0.

files.note: Adds the close-before-first-reply error to get_screen and the older-daemon warning to get_log, and rewrites the comment on explain_daemon_failure to name trip log as the exception.

checks.text: Read the daemon's GetScreen handler: in both modes it writes ScreenData or Error before it closes, and in watch mode it writes the first screen before it subscribes, so first is false by the time a session ends.

Against a current daemon this prints nothing, because its record names the client's version. The e2e script checks both sides: an empty log from a real daemon has empty stderr, and the fake older daemon's stderr is exactly the older-daemon line.
trip shutdown also treats a close as success, printing daemon stopped, but Shutdown is a unit variant every daemon decodes, so the comment's claim holds for requests an older daemon can refuse.

groups.title: Switching back after a mismatched upgrade
groups.kicker: The mismatch error says the build is current and gives the way back.
intro: trip upgrade runs the release's own install.sh and then checks what ~/.local/bin/trip --version reports. By the time that check fails, the installer has already switched current to the new build. So before it runs the installer, upgrade reads the version current names, as replaced. The installer moves previous only when it installs a different version, so replaced is the one version the upgrade can have switched away from.

1. The build reports replaced. The installer reinstalled the running version over itself, as a tag cut without a version bump does. The error says it is still current and gives no command.
  2. replaced is another version whose directory exists. The error gives ln -sfn <replaced> ~/.local/share/trip/current to switch back.
  3. Otherwise, as with no current link, the error says the build is now current.

files.note: Reads current before the installer runs and picks one of three endings for the mismatch error.

checks.text: Re-derived the case the first review flagged, trip 0.2.0 running with previous -> 0.1.0 and a tag v0.3.0 that builds 0.2.0. replaced is 0.2.0, equal to installed, so the error ends trip 0.2.0 is still current with no command. The e2e case for a build of the running version checks the same thing.
Compared with link_version in install.sh: both reduce an absolute target to its last path component.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: End-to-end checks for both messages, and the README's Upgrading section.
intro: tests/upgrade_e2e.py runs the release binary in a temporary HOME. Its fake installer now moves current and previous the way install.sh does, and release_install lays out an install of the client's own version. The script now checks:

• the three mismatch endings: switch back to the replaced version, still current, and no install before;
  • trip screen and trip log against the fake older daemon;
  • trip screen --watch of a session that ends, and an empty trip log, against a real current daemon.

checks.text: Ran python3 tests/upgrade_e2e.py on the head: it ends with all upgrade checks passed. The code at the earlier head gives a switch-back to 0.0.9 in this case, so this check catches the bug the first review found.
The session sleeps 2 seconds before it exits, so the watch must connect within that time. If it connects later, the session may already be gone and the check fails with not found.

files.note: Describes the switch-back command and the still-current case, and says that trip log prints the older-daemon line to stderr and exits 0.
